segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. Let's do a quick retro on the September release.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Sounds good. I'll start with what went well, if that's okay.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Please, go ahead.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: So the migration to the new billing service went smoother than expected. We budgeted three days and it took two.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: That's great. Was that because of the staging environment we set up last month?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Exactly. Having a realistic staging environment with production-like data caught two edge cases before they hit customers.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Good, that validates the investment. What about the on call rotation? I heard there were some pages overnight.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yeah, there were four pages between Tuesday and Thursday. Three were false alarms from a noisy health check.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: And the fourth?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: The fourth was real. The payment webhook retried too aggressively and briefly overloaded the database connection pool.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Do we have a fix for that already, or is it still open?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: We shipped a fix on Friday. We added exponential backoff and capped retries at five attempts.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Perfect. Let's make sure that's documented in the runbook so the next on call engineer isn't caught off guard.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Agreed, I'll update the runbook this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Let's talk about the frontend rollout next. How did the feature flag rollout go?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: We rolled out to five percent, then twenty five percent, then everyone, over about four days.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Any issues at each stage?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: At the twenty five percent stage we saw a small increase in checkout abandonment, maybe half a percent.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Did we figure out why?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: It turned out to be a rendering delay on older Android devices. The new checkout summary component was doing a synchronous layout calculation.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Was that fixed before we went to a hundred percent?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yes, we moved the calculation off the main thread and abandonment went back to baseline within a day.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Nice catch. What about the design team's feedback on the new checkout flow?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Overall positive. They want to revisit the confirmation screen typography in the next design review.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Let's put that on the agenda for next week rather than block this release on it.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Agreed, it's a small polish item, not a blocker.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Okay, now for what didn't go well. I want to talk about the deployment pipeline delays.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Right, the pipeline took almost forty minutes on release day, compared to our usual fifteen.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Do we know the root cause?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: The test suite for the reporting module isn't parallelized, and it grew significantly this quarter.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: How many tests are we talking about?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: About twelve hundred tests now, up from around four hundred at the start of the year.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: That's a big jump. Should we split that suite out, or invest in parallelization?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: I'd recommend parallelization first since it's lower effort. Splitting can come later if needed.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Let's put together a small proposal by next Friday and estimate the effort.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: I can own that. I'll have a short write up ready by Wednesday for early feedback.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Great, thank you. Any other blockers or risks we should flag before we wrap up?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: One thing. The vendor for the fraud detection API mentioned a rate limit change starting next month.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Do we know the new limit yet?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Not the exact number, but they said it could be as much as forty percent lower than today.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Let's get that confirmed this week so we have time to adjust our request batching if needed.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: I'll email them today and loop in the team once I hear back.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: One more thing before we wrap. How's the team feeling about the on call load in general?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Honestly, a bit better than last quarter. Splitting the rotation into two weeks instead of one helped a lot.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Good, I was worried burnout might creep back in after the holidays.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: It's manageable right now. The main ask from the team was better documentation for the newer services.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: That's fair. Let's fold that into the runbook update you're already doing.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: I can do that. I'll flag which services are missing docs and prioritize those first.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Great. Last item, budget for next quarter. Do we need to request more infrastructure spend?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Slightly. The staging environment upgrade added about eight percent to our monthly cloud bill.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Is that within the range we planned for?

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yes, it's under the ten percent ceiling we agreed on back in July.

segments.speaker: Alex
segments.text: Perfect. I think that covers everything. Thanks for a thorough retro, Jordan.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Thanks, Alex. Talk soon.
